confirmed: Criterion 3 and scored_on_output true hold for all six outcomes. The scores come from participants' own AUT responses: 'Two trained independent raters, who had established reliability using pilot data, scored all responses independently.' Locator: p. 3, Section 2.2.

No listed outcome is self-reported. Affiliative bonding, interaction quality, usefulness, ease of use, and learning intentions are questionnaire ratings, and the form correctly leaves them out. Locator: p. 3, Section 2.2; pp. 6-7, Section 3.2.

Measure codes fit the paper's definitions. Fluency is 'the total number of valid, non-redundant ideas produced' and flexibility counts 'distinct conceptual categories represented in a participant's responses' (category_count). Originality is a 1-5 rating of each idea by the two raters (human_raters). The paper does not call the raters experts. Forms c041, c047, and c094 also code unspecified trained raters as human_raters (c166 differs). Locator: p. 3, Section 2.2.

ai_available_when_produced no and question after_ai are supported. The assigned condition belongs to the instruction phase ('The instructional phase lasted approximately 8-10 min, during which participants in each group experienced their assigned condition'), the chat session 'lasted approximately 8 to10 min', and Fig. 1B puts 'Post-test 10min' after 'Instruction & Learning 8 - 10min' and a 60-s rest. The paper does not say in words that ChatGPT was closed during the post-test, and the form's open_questions already say so. Locator: p. 4, Section 2.3 and Fig. 1B; pp. 4-5, Section 2.4.
timing immediate: one session, 'with a 60s break between each part'. Locator: p. 4, Fig. 1 caption and Fig. 1B.

Constructs are right. Originality is novelty, the idea count is fluency, and the category count within one person's responses is flexibility, not diversity. The paper computes no similarity across people. Locator: p. 3, Section 2.2.

Unit participant is right: 'Their ratings were then averaged to yield each participant's fluency, originality, and flexibility scores', and every creativity ANOVA has F(2,92), that is, 95 people in three groups. Locator: p. 3, Section 2.2; pp. 5-6, Section 3.1.

Identical-item numbers match the PDF text layer. Interactions: fluency F(2,92) = 3.10, p = 0.050, η2p = 0.06. Originality 6.12, p = 0.003, η2p = 0.12. Flexibility 4.01, p = 0.021, η2p = 0.08. Instruction main effect on originality 3.46, p = 0.036, η2p = 0.12, others ps ≥ 0.127. AI post-test fluency 11.29 ± 2.91, originality 34.91 ± 10.80, flexibility 7.29 ± 2.97. AI vs human and control ps ≤ 0.04. Control originality p = 0.064, fluency and flexibility ps ≤ 0.021. Locator: p. 5, Section 3.1 Learning outcome; p. 6, Section 3.1.

Novel-item numbers match. Interactions: flexibility F(2,92) = 7.182, p = 0.001, η2p = 0.14. Fluency 1.83, p = 0.167. Originality 2.02, p = 0.139. Instruction main effect on flexibility 3.69, p = 0.029, η2p = 0.07, others ps ≥ 0.144. AI post-test fluency 9.05 ± 2.63, originality 30.83 ± 10.32, flexibility 9.67 ± 3.40, ps ≤ 0.009. AI flexibility vs human and control ps ≤ 0.002. Human originality p = 0.001, fluency and flexibility ps ≥ 0.115. Locator: p. 6, Section 3.1 Transfer outcome.

Fig. 2 annotations, read from a 4x render of the page, match every contrast. 2A has only within-arm brackets (p < 0.001 each). 2B: AI post vs Human post p = 0.04, vs Control post p < 0.001. 2C: 0.04 and 0.003, control pre-post p = 0.02. 2D: AI pre-post p = 0.0092 only. 2E: AI pre-post p < 0.0001, Human pre-post p = 0.0013, AI post vs Control post p = 0.0230. 2F: AI post vs Human post p = 0.002, vs Control post p < 0.001. Locator: p. 6, Fig. 2.

Directions follow the evidence. treatment_higher rests on a printed or annotated AI post-test advantage. no_clear_difference applies where Fig. 2 has no between-arm bracket, and the caption says 'Significant differences from multiple comparisons are annotated with p-values within the figure.' Locator: p. 6, Fig. 2 and caption; pp. 5-6, Section 3.1.

statistics_available follows the form spec. Only the AI arm's post-test means and SDs are printed, so arm_means_sds_ns is correctly absent. p_value_only appears only in the seven contrasts that have a pairwise p. Locator: pp. 5-6, Section 3.1; p. 6, Fig. 2.

comparison_type is right. The control 'sat quietly with their eyes closed for the same duration, without engaging in any instructional activity or interaction' (ai_vs_bau), and the human arm had a trained human instructor (ai_vs_active). Locator: p. 4, Section 2.3.

primary not_stated is right. The paper lists the three scores together ('Dependent variables included fluency, originality, and flexibility scores derived from the AUTs') and mentions no preregistration. Locator: p. 5, Section 3.1.

The form's flag on 7.29 ± 2.97 holds. In Fig. 2C the AI post-test bar sits near 10 and the AI pre-test bar near 7 with an SD bar of about 3, while the other five printed AI post-test means agree with their bars. The form records the value as printed, as the spec requires. Locator: p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 6, Fig. 2C.

A paper-side inconsistency that the form correctly records as printed: η2p = 0.12 for the identical-item originality main effect does not fit F(2,92) = 3.46, which implies about 0.07. Locator: p. 5, Section 3.1 Learning outcome.

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The chat logs were recorded but not scored, no output was scored with AI available, and no measure compares different people. Change scores enter only brain-behavior correlations across all participants. The other measures are self-reports or fNIRS. Locator: pp. 3-5, Sections 2.2-2.6; pp. 6-8, Sections 3.2-3.5.
summary: Criterion 3 holds: all six outcomes are fluency, originality, and flexibility scores that two trained raters gave to participants' own AUT responses in a post-test phase after the 8-10 min ChatGPT session, which supports after_ai, the constructs, the measures, and the participant unit. Every printed number and every Fig. 2 annotation in the twelve contrasts matches the PDF, no eligible outcome is missing, and the only inference left is that the paper places AI use in the instruction phase without saying in words that ChatGPT was closed during the post-test, which the form already flags.
